== Biography ==

Peter is one of four young rabbits living in a sand-bank beneath the root of a great fir-tree. He is distinguished from his siblings—Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail—by his impulsive nature and fondness for mischief, rather than the good behavior and obedience of the others.

While his siblings went down the lane to gather blackberries, Peter's nature led him in an entirely different direction: straight to Mr. McGregor's garden. He squeezed beneath the gate and began eating the vegetables within—lettuces and French beans, followed by radishes. Excess soon overtook appetite; feeling sick from eating too much, he ventured further into the garden searching for parsley to settle his distress.

His trespass came to an abrupt end when he encountered Mr. McGregor, engaged in planting young cabbages. The farmer's response was swift and hostile. He rose, pursued Peter through the garden with a rake, and cried out "Stop thief!" Peter's courage abandoned him entirely; seized by dreadful fear, he ran in all directions through the garden in blind panic, his distress so great that the path by which he had entered—the gate through which he might escape—became lost to him.

== Narrative role ==

Peter is one of four rabbits—alongside [[Flopsy]], Mopsy, and Cotton-tail—who live with their Mother in a sand-bank beneath the root of a very big fir-tree.

One day, while his three siblings, who were good little bunnies, went down the lane to gather blackberries, Peter, who was very naughty, ran straight away to Mr. [[McGregor]]'s garden and squeezed under the gate. Inside the garden, he ate some lettuces and some French beans, and then some radishes. Feeling rather sick after his feast, he went to look for some parsley.

Round the end of a cucumber frame, Peter encountered Mr. McGregor, who was on his hands and knees planting out young cabbages. Mr. McGregor jumped up and ran after Peter, waving a rake and calling out, "Stop thief!" Peter was most dreadfully frightened; he rushed all over the garden, for he had forgotten the way back to the gate.

Presently, Peter sneezed—'Kertyschoo!'

== Personality ==

Peter is willful and disobedient. Set against his siblings—Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cotton-tail, who are "good little bunnies"—Peter is emphatically "very naughty." He is quick to disregard his mother's warnings, marked by an impulsive and daring disposition.

Yet his courage proves fragile when confronted with true danger. Upon Mr. McGregor's pursuit, Peter becomes "most dreadfully frightened." His fear unmakes him entirely: he rushes about in confusion, unable to remember even the path by which he entered. This portrait of contradictions—bold in transgression, yet brittle in peril—reveals a character whose naughtiness masks a fundamental vulnerability.

== Trivia ==

* Peter demonstrated a determined appetite, consuming lettuces, French beans, and radishes in rapid succession, with parsley sought afterward to soothe his troubled stomach.
* An involuntary sneeze—'Kertyschoo!'—escaped him during his flight from the garden.
